value: Snapshot: the id set of rows in CLEAR_FINISHED_SNAPSHOT_STATUSES is snapshotted ONCE before the first request; a job that reaches Done mid-run is not swept.
Independence: one DELETE /{id} per snapshotted id, each request independent of the others.
Continue on failure: a failed or 404 response never aborts the fan-out; every snapshotted id is attempted EXACTLY ONCE.
Successes kept: confirmed deletions are never rolled back.
Files: media files stay on disk - the API removes the queue record only.
Reconcile: EXACTLY ONE list refetch after the fan-out settles; the refetch, not local optimistic state, is what the list renders.
Report: the G35 partial-result toast states the removed count, the failed-or-skipped count, AND a reason per failure.
CLEAR_FINISHED_SEMANTICS.note: All seven clauses are normative; each maps to at least one AC.

BULK_ENDPOINT_POLICY.value: Client-side fan-out only. POST /{queue}/bulk DOES NOT EXIST and may not be invented. Every bulk action issues the existing per-id request N times under CLEAR_FINISHED_SEMANTICS.

SELECTION_MODEL.value: Selection state is a Set<string> of job ids held by the page. Plain click toggles one; Shift+click selects the inclusive range from the last-clicked anchor in current render order; Ctrl/Cmd+A selects every row in the FILTERED list. Selection is cleared on queue identity change and after a bulk action completes.

ERROR_SURFACE.value: Every failed API call surfaces a user-visible message (G15). Silent catch is forbidden. Partial bulk failures use the G35 partial-result toast.

PAUSE_SCOPE.value: Pause/Resume act on the queue PROCESSOR, not on individual jobs. The toggle reflects ProcessorState (Idle | Processing | Paused).

G32_RULE.note: Corrected during execution review round 1 (Finding 5). The plan originally recorded this entry's value as 'Interactive targets are at least 44x44 CSS px.', which is not what the cited source says and is not stated anywhere in the repo: emerging-standards.md G32 is the no-raw-hex token rule, and no G-standard, docs/build-plan/10-queue-card-ui.md, or ADR names a 44px hit target. Every AC that cites G32_RULE (AC-45.3, AC-45.10, AC-46.6, AC-47.4, AC-47.5, AC-47.5a, AC-45.19, AC-45.19a, AC-46.14) tests the token rule, as did MEU-43/44 before them; the value string was the only artefact carrying the 44px claim. SELECTION_HEADER_CONTRACT.value: A header SelectionCheckbox sits above the list at all times (independent of BULK_BAR_ACTIONS visibility). It is checked when every filtered row is selected, INDETERMINATE when some are, unchecked when none are, and carries an "N items" count. Toggling it selects/deselects the FILTERED list, not the unfiltered queue.

SELECTION_PRIMITIVE_EXTENSION.value: SelectionCheckbox.onChange is `(checked: boolean) => void` and its onClick calls stopPropagation (ui/src/renderer/src/components/ui/SelectionCheckbox.tsx:16,63-78), and QueueCard.onSelectChange is `(id, checked) => void` (QueueCard.tsx:93,282-289). Neither forwards modifier state, so SELECTION_MODEL's Shift+click range select has NO production path today. Both signatures are widened in this project to forward a `{ shiftKey: boolean }` modifiers object, and both files are in MEU-47's Files Modified inventory.
SELECTION_PRIMITIVE_EXTENSION.source: Local Canon - direct file read, 2026-09-02 (plan-review round 1, Finding 2).
SELECTION_PRIMITIVE_EXTENSION.note: Widening is additive: the modifiers argument is optional at the call site, so existing callers keep compiling.

REORDER_WIRE_CONTRACT.value: PUT /conversions/reorder and PUT /downloads/reorder accept `{ job_ids: string[] }` - a COMPLETE permutation of the queue - and 422 on any other body (packages/api/src/avkit_api/routes/conversions.py:232-239, routes/downloads.py:210-217). There is no `{id, direction}` shape. The permutation is built by the EXISTING exported `buildReorderBody(ids, selectedId, 'up'|'down'|'top'|'bottom')` (convert-controls.ts:108-128, download-controls.ts:95-115), which is reused unchanged.
REORDER_WIRE_CONTRACT.source: Local Canon - direct file read, 2026-09-02 (plan-review round 1, Finding 3).

BULK_REORDER_ALGORITHM.value: Bulk Move to top / Move to bottom is a SEQUENTIAL fold under BULK_ENDPOINT_POLICY: starting from the current order, for each selected id in render order (reversed for move-top so relative order is preserved) compute the next permutation with buildReorderBody against the order produced by the PRECEDING SUCCESSFUL call, PUT it, and only then compute the next. A failed step does not abort the remainder (CLEAR_FINISHED_SEMANTICS clause 3 applies), but the next step folds from the last order the server actually accepted, never from the stale initial order.
BULK_REORDER_ALGORITHM.source: Research-backed (plan-review round 1, Finding 3) - the reorder endpoint takes an absolute permutation, so stale-based fan-out would clobber earlier steps.
BULK_REORDER_ALGORITHM.note: Asserted by a unit test that issues N requests and checks each body is the fold of the previous, plus a test where step 2 fails and step 3 still folds from step 1's accepted order.

EMPTY_STATE_CONTRACT.value:
Per page, because the two queues have DIFFERENT intake contracts.
CONVERTER (file intake): with items=[] QueueList renders EmptyDropZone (testid queue-empty-dropzone) - dashed drop target, the microcopy "Drop video or audio files here - or", and a prominent Browse... button (browseTestId queue-empty-browse, the EmptyDropZone prop at EmptyDropZone.tsx:190) as an equal path; with items it keeps the drag-over overlay PLUS the compact "Drop files to add" strip (testid queue-drop-strip). onBrowse and onDropFiles BOTH route to the page's EXISTING production intake - window.api.showFilesDialog(CONVERT_DIALOG_FILTERS) feeding the same `staging` state that backs the current convert-browse button (ConvertPage.tsx:470-484). No new picker, no no-op callback. The page's EXISTING staging drop zone and its convert-browse button are untouched - that is the pre-queue staging surface, a different surface from the queue's empty state; the two share the handler, not the testid.
DOWNLOADER (URL intake): there is NO local-file intake path and Phase 10 adds no new REST surface, so the file drop/Browse invitation does NOT apply. With items=[] the page renders queue-empty-invite - the microcopy "Paste a video link above to queue a download" and a real button (queue-empty-invite-action) that focuses the existing url-input. That is an observable production outcome (document.activeElement is url-input, and typing + add-btn produces the normal POST /downloads), not a placeholder. No queue-empty-dropzone and no queue-drop-strip on this page.
EMPTY_STATE_CONTRACT.source: Spec - docs/build-plan/10-queue-card-ui.md:259-274 (Empty state and drop targets) for the converter; Local Canon for the downloader split - the same spec's Scope and non-goals says Phase 10 "changes presentation and one service contract (re-queue widening); it adds no new REST surface", and DownloaderPage's only intake is addFromForm() reading url-input (DownloaderPage.tsx:156-170), so a file Drop/Browse surface there could only be a no-op or an invented endpoint.
EMPTY_STATE_CONTRACT.note: Round 1 Finding 4: QueueList currently returns a bare <div> with only the hover overlay when items=[] (QueueList.tsx:77-104), and neither EmptyDropZone (built in MEU-44, still unmounted) nor the non-empty strip was scheduled by any AC - so the migration would have shipped a blank panel where both tables render an empty-state row today. Round 2 Finding F12: the round-1 correction generalised the converter's file-drop invitation to BOTH pages, which the downloader cannot honour - corrected to the per-page contract above. Widening the downloader to local-file intake would need a new REST surface and is out of scope for Phase 10; it is not deferred to a scheduled MEU because no build-plan row asks for it.

MOUNT_GATE_PHASE_SCOPES.value:
Which (page, retired-id, home) obligations each -Scope of MOUNT_GATE_SCRIPT enforces. A home is obligated once the MEU named in its `meu` field has shipped:
  -Scope convert    (MEU-45 gate): every home whose meu is MEU-45. Homes whose meu is MEU-47 are PENDING - the gate prints them under a `PENDING (MEU-47)` heading and exits 0, but it may not silently omit them, and a MEU-45 home that fails still fails the gate.
  -Scope downloader (MEU-46 gate): the same rule with MEU-46.
  -Scope all        (MEU-47 gate and phase exit): EVERY home in RETIRED_TOOLBAR_CONTROLS is obligated independently, regardless of meu. There are no alternatives at this scope - a working `kebab move-top` does NOT satisfy `bulk-move-top`. The PENDING list must be empty; a non-empty PENDING list at -Scope all is a gate failure.
MOUNT_GATE_PHASE_SCOPES.note: Without the phase split, either the MEU-45/46 gates fail on controls that do not exist yet, or the final gate accepts a dead MEU-47 control because its sibling home works. Both were real: round 1's flat map produced the first, round 1's correction produced the second.

BULK_CONTROL_E2E_OBLIGATION.value: Every control MEU-47 introduces gets its own E2E interaction + outcome assertion, on BOTH pages - none may rely on a sibling home or on registration alone: each of the five BULK_BAR_ACTIONS (bulk-retry -> asserts the intercepted re-queue requests; bulk-move-top and bulk-move-bottom -> assert the intercepted REORDER_WIRE_CONTRACT body and the resulting card order; bulk-remove -> confirm then assert the rows are gone; bulk-clear-selection -> asserts the bar disappears and every checkbox is unchecked), the queue-select-all header checkbox in all three SELECTION_HEADER_CONTRACT states, and the keyboard selection entry path (focus a card, toggle its SelectionCheckbox by keyboard, assert the bar appears).
BULK_CONTROL_E2E_OBLIGATION.source: Research-backed (plan-review round 2, Finding F4) + Local Canon E2_RULE.
BULK_CONTROL_E2E_OBLIGATION.note: Round 2 Finding F4: AC-47.10 exercised only bulk Remove and Clear finished, so bulk Retry, Move top, Move bottom and Clear selection had no required assertion anywhere - and the assertion census cannot protect a capability that never had one.
